e-16516.knowledge_point: Computing the Value of a Function of a Jordan Block
e-16516.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and a Jordan block $J_n(\lambda),$ we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072904/assets/738039128c2eef5b848f6114c6008188456705206879411c9dab82e919bc18b5.png)

In this case, we have $f(x) = 2^{x},$ $n=4,$ and $\lambda=1.$

Since $n=4,$ we need to compute the first $4-1=3$ derivatives of $f{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={2}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & ={2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & ={2}^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2} \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & ={2}^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{4}(1)) & =[\begin{aligned}f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) & \frac{1}{2!}{f}^{″}(1) & \frac{1}{3!}{f}^{‴}(1) \\ 0 & f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) & \frac{1}{2!}{f}^{″}(1) \\ 0 & 0 & f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & f(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{2}^{1} & {2}^{1}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & \frac{1}{2}\cdot {2}^{1}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2} & \frac{1}{6}\cdot {2}^{1}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{3} \\ 0 & {2}^{1} & {2}^{1}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & \frac{1}{2}\cdot {2}^{1}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2} \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{1} & {2}^{1}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & {2}^{1}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & (\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2} & \frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{3} \\ 0 & 2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & (\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
f({J}_{n}(\lambda ))=[\begin{aligned}f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & \frac{{f}^{″}(\lambda )}{2!} & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-1)}(\lambda )}{(n-1)!} \\ 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-2)}(\lambda )}{(n-2)!} \\ ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) \\ 0 & ⋯ & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda )\end{aligned}].

In this case, we have $f(x)={3}^{x},$ $n=2,$ and $\lambda =1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={3}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & ={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{2}(1)) & =[\begin{aligned}f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) \\ 0 & f(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{3}^{1} & {3}^{1}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ 0 & {3}^{1}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\sqrt{{J}_{3}(4)}=\,\,$ |  | $0$ | {{field-4}} | {{field-5}} |  |
|  |  | $0$ | $0$ | {{field-6}} |  |
content.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and a Jordan block ${J}_{n}(\lambda ),$ we have

$$
f({J}_{n}(\lambda ))=[\begin{aligned}f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & \frac{{f}^{″}(\lambda )}{2!} & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-1)}(\lambda )}{(n-1)!} \\ 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-2)}(\lambda )}{(n-2)!} \\ ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) \\ 0 & ⋯ & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda )\end{aligned}].
$$

In this case, we have $f(x)=\sqrt{x},$ $n=3,$ and $\lambda =4.$

Since $n=3,$ we need to compute the first $3-1=2$ derivatives of $f:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\sqrt{x}={x}^{1/2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{4x\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{3}(2)) & =[\begin{aligned}f(4) & {f}^{′}(4) & \frac{{f}^{″}(4)}{2!} \\ 0 & f(4) & {f}^{′}(4) \\ 0 & 0 & f(4)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{4} & \frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}} & -\frac{1}{2\cdot 4\cdot 4\sqrt{4}} \\ 0 & \sqrt{4} & \frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}} \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{64} \\ 0 & 2 & \frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
